answer: New identities lock a 70,000 POA copper bond into a saffron-stamped ledger: every work proof must echo through three random peers, each re-checking the original task before forwarding it — an echo that differs from the source breaks the chain. A forged echo burns the bond, half to the reporter, the identity banned 12 epochs and its saffron seal revoked. Forging 1,000 fake identities costs 1,000 × 70,000 = 70,000,000 POA, while an honest agent pays one 70,000 POA bond once. The limit: echo chains slow honest agents whose work is hard to re-check quickly.
